results.title: What is going wrong in Tamil Nadu’s SIR? | Focus Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/state: Issues in Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process for voter rolls.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Tamil Nadu is facing operational failures, potentially leading to the mass deletion of genuine voters before the 2026 elections.
notes.fact_box: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a periodic exercise by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to update and clean voter rolls. In Tamil Nadu, the process is currently criticized for unrealistic deadlines and confusing documentation, risking the disenfranchisement of eligible voters.

prelims_pointers.text: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is the constitutional body responsible for the preparation and revision of electoral rolls.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a periodic exercise to ensure the accuracy of the voter list.
The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of a state oversees the implementation of the SIR at the state level.

notes.mains_question: Discuss the importance of maintaining an accurate and inclusive electoral roll in a democracy. How can administrative inefficiencies in voter list revisions impact the principle of Universal Adult Franchise?
mains_dimensions: Administrative bottleneck: Unrealistic deadlines and lack of clear instructions leading to procedural errors in voter list maintenance.
Disenfranchisement risk: Potential deletion of genuine voters due to confusing documentation, undermining the right to vote.
Technological gap: Need for robust digital verification to replace manual, error-prone revision processes.

results.reason: elections_process/national: EC's authority on citizenship scrutiny and electoral roll revision rules.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) submitted an affidavit to the Supreme Court clarifying that its power to scrutinize citizenship for electoral rolls is distinct from the Union Government's exclusive power to termi…
notes.fact_box: The ECI cited Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, which grants the Centre exclusive authority to determine the termination of Indian citizenship upon voluntary acquisition of foreign nationality. The ECI argued its scrutiny is limited to verifying eligibility for the electoral roll under Article 326.

prelims_pointers.text: Article 324: Empowers the Election Commission to supervise and control the conduct of elections.
Article 326: Specifies that every person registered in the electoral roll is entitled to vote, with Indian citizenship as a prerequisite.
Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955: Deals with the termination of Indian citizenship in cases of voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.
Representation of the People Act (ROPA), 1950: Governs the preparation and revision of electoral rolls.

notes.mains_question: Examine the constitutional boundaries between the Election Commission's plenary powers under Article 324 and the Union Government's exclusive jurisdiction over citizenship status.
